summary_md:
# Stigande ränteoro – Shein faller i börsdebuten

**Feed**: efn-borsfrukost  
**Published**: 2026-09-01  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

EFN Morgon, with AMF portfolio manager Patricia Hedelius as guest, focused on renewed worry about rising long-term interest rates (Japanese 10-year yields above 3%) and Shein's weak debut on the Hong Kong exchange, set against brighter consumer and industrial signs: Puuilo's positive profit warning, a strong Swedish PMI at 56.1 and SEB's strong earnings forecasts. The guest is positive on Thule, Volvo Cars, Balder, Scandic/Pandox and Epiroc. She is cautious on H&M, holding back on EQT because of rates and a slow exit market, and sceptical of Boliden's South American zinc deal. Property discounts and share buybacks, led by Castellum, were another theme.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 VOLCAR-B — Volvo Cars | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 80%

The AMF guest owns it and emphatically says it's the auto stock to own, thanks to strong launched products and brand credibility.

#### Reasoning

The guest (AMF) says Volvo Cars has a very strong position despite a tough global car market, Chinese exports and weak North America and Germany. Its products are already launched and demand is strong. Polestar exposure is limited: ~$1.5bn of $35bn revenue, plus a ~$600m loan. Geely ties are seen as strategically valuable.

#### Sell Triggers

- Polestar closure triggers loan write-downs or cost-sharing losses
- Geely capital-allocation stress spills over
- Weaker demand for new models
- Governance problems around the chair change

> *"Jag skulle vilja hävda med emfas att Volvo Cars... Om du är intresserad av bilaktier så är det där du ska vara."*

---

### 🟢 THULE — Thule | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

AMF is the largest owner and believes strongly in its R&D; it is waiting for the consumer, especially in North America, to recover.

#### Reasoning

The guest's fund is Thule's largest owner and has strong conviction in its product-segment R&D. Near-term headwinds are a weak North American mid-market consumer and soft car and housing activity, while Europe holds up. The thesis is a consumer recovery lifting outdoor spending.

#### Sell Triggers

- North American consumer stays weak
- The bike market fails to normalise
- Europe's consumer weakens

> *"AMF är ju största ägare i Thule sen ett par år. Vi tror starkt på den RND och sånt som man gör inom sina olika produktsegment."*

---

### 🟢 BALD-B — Balder | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 70%

AMF raised its stake this summer: buybacks intensified, and every deal is weighed against buying back its own stock at a 40-50% discount.

#### Reasoning

The guest prefers Balder among property stocks because it stepped up buybacks after the half-year report and measures each property deal against repurchasing its discounted shares. She sees large buyback potential over the next 12 months, narrowing the discount to NAV, following Castellum's model.

#### Sell Triggers

- Buyback program slows or stops
- Rates rise sharply toward 5%
- Discount widens on balance-sheet concerns

> *"Vi har valt Balder, för vi flaggade upp i Balder i somras. De har intensifierat sitt återköps program sen halvårsrapporten."*

---

### 🟢 SHOT — Scandic | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

AMF owns it: record Stockholm tourism, willingness to pay for experiences, low hotel construction, and Airbnb less competitive.

#### Reasoning

The guest's fund owns a fair amount of Scandic. Demand for hotel stays and European travel is strong, new hotel supply is low, and Airbnb's price edge is fading. Together these support occupancy and pricing.

#### Sell Triggers

- Travel demand weakens
- A new wave of hotel construction
- Consumer spending slowdown

> *"Man äger en hel del i Scandic också. ... Vi ser också att nybyggnationen av hotell har varit ganska låg."*

---

### 🟢 PNDX-B — Pandox | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 55%

AMF owns it; the hotel-property owner benefits from record tourism and low new supply.

#### Reasoning

The host notes the guest owns Pandox, and the guest agrees the tourism and low hotel-supply trends benefit both Scandic and Pandox.

#### Sell Triggers

- Tourism declines
- Higher rates pressure property valuations

> *"Kul för Scandic, hotelloperatören och Pandox, fastighetsoperatören. Ja, precis."*

---

### 🟢 EPI-A — Epiroc | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 60%

AMF owns a lot; it won a SEK 610m Botswana order. Suggested as a picks-and-shovels alternative to Boliden.

#### Reasoning

The guest confirms a large holding. She suggests Epiroc and Sandvik as mining exposure without Boliden's acquisition and governance risks. The new SEK 610m aftermarket and service order supports the thesis.

#### Sell Triggers

- Mining capex slowdown
- Order intake weakens

> *"Ja, vi äger en hel del av Epiroc. Vill du inte spela Boliden så har du både Epiroc och Sandvik att titta på."*

---

### 🟠 SAND — Sandvik | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Suggested with Epiroc as an alternative mining-equipment play instead of Boliden.

#### Reasoning

The guest mentions Sandvik as an alternative way to get mining exposure. No explicit holding or conviction was stated.

#### Sell Triggers

- Mining equipment demand falls

> *"Vill du inte spela Boliden så har du både Epiroc och Sandvik att titta på."*

---

### ⛔ HM-B — H&M | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 65%

AMF has exited: profitability improved but top-line growth is not coming, and it struggles to attract customers. Guest is wait-and-see.

#### Reasoning

The guest's fund sold its H&M position. H&M improved margins but lacks sales growth, possibly because its offer fails to attract customers. Shein's struggles and a cyclical view add to the caution.

#### Sell Triggers

- Top-line growth reaccelerates
- Clear improvement in customer traction

> *"Vi äger inte nu, för nu har vi gått ut. ... Vi är nog lite mer avvaktande till H&M i det här fallet."*

---

### 🟡 EQT — EQT | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 60%

AMF is invested but more cautious about adding because rates are rising and the exit market is sluggish: 'more hold'.

#### Reasoning

The guest owns EQT and notes it lacks the private-credit problems peers have, yet it has been priced as if it had them. Rising rates and slow exits make her reluctant to add, so she holds. Shares fell 3.7% on the day.

#### Sell Triggers

- Rates keep rising toward 5%
- Exit market stays frozen
- Private-credit contagion from peers like Partners Group

> *"så tror jag att man kanske är lite mer försiktigt inställd till att investera nytt, mer hold på det."*

---

### 🟡 BOL — Boliden | **HOLD** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Guest is sceptical of the South American zinc acquisition and would have preferred buybacks or dividends; she concedes it adds growth.

#### Reasoning

The guest questions whether Boliden is becoming a mining conglomerate. She says investors could buy zinc assets directly and would rather see buybacks or dividends from the strong balance sheet. Governance and oversight in South America are harder. On the positive side, zinc is at a 4-year high and the deal adds growth.

#### Sell Triggers

- Acquisition integration issues
- Further non-core M&A
- Smelter margins squeezed by fast zinc price rises

> *"vi skulle nog hellre sett att man köpte helägda tillgångar ... hade man ju inte heller ... spottat i glaset om man hade fått en del i återköp eller utdelningar"*

---
